ai.description: The Assam Roofed Turtle reaches 20 cm. It features a high, serrated vertebral keel and a dark olive-brown carapace with a yellow stripe. The plastron is yellow with large, dark central blotches.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Assam Roofed Turtle is best distinguished by the prominent, black, saw-toothed keel running along the center of its olive-brown carapace, which is more serrated than others.
ai.habitat: The Assam Roofed Turtle inhabits fast-flowing, clear-water hill streams and rivers with rocky beds, typically found at low to moderate altitudes in the Brahmaputra basin.
ai.behavior: The Assam Roofed Turtle is primarily diurnal, often seen basking on logs or rocks along riverbanks to regulate its body temperature during the day.
ai.reproductionNotes: The Assam Roofed Turtle is oviparous, laying a clutch of 6–12 eggs. Breeding occurs during the dry season, typically from February to April in northeastern India.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Assam Roofed Turtle is endemic to the Brahmaputra and Meghna river basins, occurring in Assam and Arunachal Pradesh at elevations below 200 meters.
